newsitem.title: USA: Outlet malls good for holiday shoppers.
newsitem.headline: Outlet malls good for holiday shoppers.

text.p: For one thing, leading manufacturers' and designers' outlet divisions are heavily stocking merchandise to reduce the guesswork in selecting the right gift, according to Tanger Outlet Centres Inc., a national developer of outlet malls.

"Our leading merchants have clearly defined that this year non-specific sizes, solid colours, individual pieces rather than collection additions, and holiday housewares are anticipated to be the hot sellers," said Carrie Johnson, vice president of marketing for Tanger Outlet.
In an outlet centre, an entire store is devoted to a single designer label vs. just a few racks in a department store for the same product.
Manufacturers open outlet stores mainly to trade off their brand names, said analysts who question whether shoppers get more for their holiday dollar.

"(Outlet stores) create an image," said Steven Kernkraut, an analyst at Bear Stearns & Co. "When you do try to match prices in outlets to stores, I don't think you're seeing a huge differential in prices, particularly when there is a sale."
The popular Chenille sweater and turtleneck at the Jones New York outlet are such examples.

"The full retail price could range from $60 to $90. The same item in the outlets are generally 25 percent off," said Dianna Lubbe of Jones New York. "But if stores are advertising a 30 percent sale, then sometimes you could get it (from a store) for less."
Discounts may rise to 40 percent, analysts and retailers have said.
Aside from price differences, outlets tend to stock merchandise in basic colours and generic small, medium and large sizes.
"We believe this back-to-the-basics approach in the outlets will offer holiday consumers the highest possible comfort level in making gift purchases," Johnson said.
Down jackets are touted as the gift of choice in men's outerwear in trendy solid navy, pine, red and gray colours.

Among tabletop manufacturers, holiday themed products such as Santa cookie plates are on full display, as well as china and crystal. In non-holiday selections, several housewares retailers have said bar ware was all the rage, particularly martini glasses.
"Its the mixed-drink thing and idea of socializing," said Myron Bush of Pottery Barn. "There are (martini) shakers of all different sizes and styles. It's not the year for the beer drinker."
He said cocktail items were the second biggest seller behind seasonal choices such as ornaments.
Consumers still at a loss for the perfect gift may find their best choice is a gift certificate.
